source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice short questions written from Chapter 9 (PDF 189-211), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh chapter 9 (Acid-Base Chemistry) ke poore chapter se practice short questions (mukhtasar sawal) hain, chapter ke sections ki tarteeb mein, Board ke 2 number wale sawal ke andaz mein. Har sawal ka mukhtasar model jawab hai; chhote numericals mein hal ke qadam hain, aur farq wale sawal ka jawab table mein hai.

blocks.prompt:
1 How do acids and bases change the colours of litmus and phenolphthalein?
(Acids aur bases litmus aur phenolphthalein ke rang kaise badalte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Acids litmus ko neele se laal aur basic phenolphthalein ko gulabi se berang karte hain. Bases litmus ko laal se neela aur phenolphthalein ko berang se gulabi karte hain.

book_ref.quote: Acids change litmus from blue to red and basic phenolphthalein from pink to colorless

blocks.prompt:
2 What is the limitation of the Arrhenius theory of acids and bases?
(Arrhenius theory ki kami (limitation) kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Arrhenius theory acid aur base ka reaction sirf aqueous (paani wale) medium mein bayan karti hai. Bohat se reactions paani ke ilawa doosre solvents mein ya baghair solvent hote hain, jin ki yeh wazahat nahi kar sakti.

book_ref.quote: There are many reactions that occur in solvents other than water or in the absence of any solvent.

blocks.prompt:
3 Define acid and base according to the Bronsted-Lowry concept.
(Bronsted-Lowry concept ke mutabiq acid aur base ki definition likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Proton-transfer reaction mein acid woh species hai jo proton (H⁺) deti hai aur base woh jo proton leti hai. Misaal: HCl (acid) H₂O (base) ko H⁺ deta hai.

book_ref.quote: According to the Bronsted–Lowry concept, an acid is the species donating a proton

blocks.prompt:
4 Identify the conjugate acid-base pairs in HCl(g) + H₂O(ℓ) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq).
(HCl(g) + H₂O(ℓ) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) mein conjugate acid-base pairs pehchanein.)
blocks.explanation: HCl (acid, proton dene wala) se us ka conjugate base Cl⁻ banta hai; H₂O (base, proton lene wala) se us ka conjugate acid H₃O⁺ banta hai. Pairs: HCl-Cl⁻ aur H₂O-H₃O⁺.

book_ref.quote: In effect, HCl (the acid) has donated the H⁺ and H₂O (the base) has accepted it.

blocks.prompt:
5 Write the reaction of ammonia with water and show which species is the conjugate acid of NH₃.
(Ammonia ka paani se reaction likhein aur batayein ke NH₃ ka conjugate acid kaun sa hai.)
blocks.explanation: NH₃(g) + H₂O(ℓ) ⇌ NH₄⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq). Paani ka H⁺ N ke lone pair se jur jata hai. NH₄⁺ NH₃ ka conjugate acid aur OH⁻ H₂O ka conjugate base hai.

book_ref.quote: An H⁺ from H₂O attaches to the N atom’s lone pair and NH₄⁺ and OH⁻ are formed.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Book mein NH₄⁺ ke neeche "Conjugate base" chhapa hai, jo ghalat hai. NH₃ ne proton liya, is liye NH₄⁺ conjugate acid hai.

blocks.prompt:
6 What is an amphoteric substance? Why is water called amphoteric?
(Amphoteric substance kya hai? Paani ko amphoteric kyun kehte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Amphoteric substance doosre reactant ke mutabiq acid ya base dono ka kaam kar sakti hai (proton kho ya le sakti hai). Paani HCl se proton leta hai (base) magar NH₃ ko proton deta hai (acid), is liye amphoteric hai.

book_ref.quote: An amphoteric substance is a species that can act as either an acid and a base

blocks.prompt:
7 How does the reaction of gaseous HCl with gaseous NH₃ show that the Bronsted-Lowry theory works without a solvent?
(Gas HCl aur gas NH₃ ka reaction kaise dikhata hai ke Bronsted-Lowry theory baghair solvent ke bhi kaam karti hai?)
blocks.explanation: HCl(g) + NH₃(g) → NH₄Cl(s). HCl NH₃ ko proton deta hai, is liye acid hai; NH₃ proton leta hai, is liye base hai, halaanke na paani hai na OH⁻ ion.

book_ref.quote: HCl is an acid because in the reaction it donates a proton to the NH₃ molecule.

blocks.prompt:
8 Using Table 9.1, give the conjugate base of HNO₃ and the conjugate acid of CO₃²⁻, with their reactions with water.
(Table 9.1 se HNO₃ ka conjugate base aur CO₃²⁻ ka conjugate acid batayein, paani ke saath un ke reactions ke saath.)
blocks.explanation:
HNO₃ + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + NO₃⁻: HNO₃ ka conjugate base NO₃⁻ hai.
H₂O + CO₃²⁻ ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + OH⁻: CO₃²⁻ ka conjugate acid HCO₃⁻ hai.

book_ref.quote: Table 9.1 Conjugate Acid-Base Pairs of Common Species

blocks.text: 9.2 Lewis concept of acids and bases

blocks.prompt:
9 Define Lewis acid and Lewis base with one example of each.
(Lewis acid aur Lewis base ki definition aik aik misaal ke saath likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Lewis acid woh species (molecule ya ion) hai jo electron pair le sakti hai, maslan BF₃ ya Ag⁺. Lewis base woh species hai jo electron pair de sakti hai, maslan NH₃ ya F⁻.

book_ref.quote: A Lewis acid is any species (molecule or ion) that can accept a pair of electrons

blocks.prompt:
10 When does a Lewis acid-base reaction occur, and what type of bond is formed?
(Lewis acid-base reaction kab hota hai aur kaun sa bond banta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Lewis acid-base reaction tab hota hai jab base acid ko electron pair deta hai. Is pair se coordinate covalent bond banta hai aur product acid-base adduct kehlata hai.

book_ref.quote: A Lewis acid-base reaction occurs when a base donates a pair of electrons to an acid.

blocks.prompt:
11 Identify the Lewis acid and Lewis base in Ag⁺ + 2NH₃ → [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ and explain the charge on the adduct.
(Ag⁺ + 2NH₃ → [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ mein Lewis acid aur Lewis base pehchanein aur adduct ke charge ki wazahat karein.)
blocks.explanation: Har NH₃ apna lone pair deta hai, is liye NH₃ Lewis base hai; Ag⁺ pairs leta hai, is liye Lewis acid hai. Baayen taraf charges ka majmooa +1 hai, is liye adduct par +1 hai.

book_ref.quote: each of two ammonia molecules, Lewis bases, donates a pair of electrons to a positively charged silver ion

blocks.prompt:
12 Write the reaction of BF₃ with a fluoride ion and give the charge on the product.
(BF₃ ka fluoride ion se reaction likhein aur product ka charge batayein.)
blocks.explanation: BF₃ + F⁻ → BF₄⁻. Boron ke sirf chhe valence electrons hain, is liye BF₃ F⁻ (Lewis base) se lone pair leta hai. Baayen taraf kul charge −1 hai, is liye adduct BF₄⁻ par bhi −1 hai.

book_ref.quote: As a result, BF₃ is a very good Lewis acid and reacts with many Lewis bases

blocks.prompt:
13 Why is pure water a poor but measurable conductor of electricity? Write the equation.
(Khalis paani bijli ka kamzor magar napne ke qabil conductor kyun hai? Equation likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
Paani khud-ba-khud (self-ionization) thora sa ionize hota hai aur bohat kam ions bante hain:
H₂O(ℓ) + H₂O(ℓ) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq)
Yeh thore se ions halka sa, napne ke qabil current le jate hain.

book_ref.quote: Water undergoes self-ionization reversibly as follows,

blocks.prompt:
14 What is the ionic product of water? Give its value at 25 °C.
(Paani ka ionic product kya hai? 25 °C par is ki qeemat batayein.)
blocks.explanation:
Constant [H₂O] ko Kc se zarb de kar Kw milta hai, jo paani ka ionic product (dissociation constant) hai:
Kw = Kc[H₂O] = [H⁺][OH⁻] = 25 °C par 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴.

book_ref.quote: Constant concentration of water is taken on L.H.S. and multiplied with Kc to get another constant called Kw.

blocks.prompt:
15 How is the concentration of water in pure water found, and why is it treated as constant?
(Khalis paani mein paani ki concentration kaise nikalti hai aur ise constant kyun maana jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: [H₂O] = 1000 g dm⁻³ ÷ 18 g mol⁻¹ = 55.5 mol dm⁻³. Paani bohat zyada miqdaar mein hai aur bohat kam molecules ionize hote hain, is liye is ki concentration taqreeban constant rehti hai.

book_ref.quote: [H₂O] in pure water may be calculated to be 1000 g dm⁻³ divided by 18 g mol⁻¹ giving 55.5 mol dm⁻³

blocks.prompt:
16 Show that [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁷ mol dm⁻³ in neutral water at 25 °C.
(Dikhayein ke 25 °C par neutral paani mein [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁷ mol dm⁻³ hai.)
blocks.explanation:
Neutral paani mein [H⁺] = [OH⁻], is liye Kw = [H⁺]² = 10⁻¹⁴.
[H⁺] = √(10⁻¹⁴) = 10⁻⁷ mol dm⁻³, aur [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁷ mol dm⁻³.

book_ref.quote: Water undergoes self-ionization reversibly as follows,

blocks.prompt:
17 What happens to Kw, [H⁺] and [OH⁻] when a few drops of a base are added to pure water at 25 °C?
(25 °C par khalis paani mein base ke chand qatre dalne se Kw, [H⁺] aur [OH⁻] par kya asar hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: [OH⁻] barh kar [H⁺] se zyada ho jata hai, is liye dono barabar nahi rehte. Kw wahi rehta hai, 25 °C par 10⁻¹⁴.

book_ref.quote: During both of these additions, the values of Kw will remain the same

blocks.prompt:
18 How does temperature affect Kw? Use values from Table 9.2.
(Temperature Kw par kya asar daalta hai? Table 9.2 ki qeematein istemal karein.)
blocks.explanation: Temperature barhne se Kw barhta hai: 0 °C par 0.11 × 10⁻¹⁴, 10 °C par 0.30 × 10⁻¹⁴, 25 °C par 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ aur 40 °C par 3.00 × 10⁻¹⁴.

book_ref.quote: The effect of temperature on Kw is shown in Table 9.2.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Book ke Table 9.2 mein powers 10¹⁴ chhapi hain; durust 10⁻¹⁴ hain.

blocks.prompt:
19 Kw of water at 40 °C is 3.00 × 10⁻¹⁴ (Table 9.2). Calculate [H⁺] in pure water at 40 °C.
(40 °C par paani ka Kw 3.00 × 10⁻¹⁴ hai (Table 9.2). 40 °C par khalis paani mein [H⁺] nikalein.)
blocks.explanation:
Khalis paani: [H⁺] = [OH⁻], is liye [H⁺]² = Kw = 3.00 × 10⁻¹⁴.
[H⁺] = √(3.00 × 10⁻¹⁴) = 1.73 × 10⁻⁷ mol dm⁻³. Paani ab bhi neutral hai kyun ke [H⁺] = [OH⁻].

book_ref.quote: Table 9.2 prints the powers as 10¹⁴.

blocks.prompt:
20 Define pH and pOH. Who introduced these terms?
(pH aur pOH ki definition likhein. Yeh istilahaat kis ne pesh keen?)
blocks.explanation: pH = −log[H⁺] aur pOH = −log[OH⁻]. Yeh 1909 mein Danish biochemist Sørensen ne pesh keen.

book_ref.quote: In 1909, Sørensen, a Danish biochemist, introduced the term pH and pOH.

blocks.prompt:
21 Why were the pH and pOH scales developed?
(pH aur pOH scales kyun banaye gaye?)
blocks.explanation: Aqueous solutions mein H⁺ aur OH⁻ ki concentrations itni kam hoti hain (maslan 10⁻⁷ mol dm⁻³) ke aasani se likhi aur hisaab mein istemal nahi hoteen, is liye log wale pH aur pOH scales banaye gaye.

book_ref.quote: the concentration of H⁺ and OH⁻ are too low to be conveniently expressed and used in calculations

blocks.prompt:
22 Show that pH + pOH = 14 at 25 °C.
(Dikhayein ke 25 °C par pH + pOH = 14 hai.)
blocks.explanation: Kw = [H⁺][OH⁻] = 10⁻¹⁴. Dono taraf −log lene se: −log[H⁺] + (−log[OH⁻]) = 14, yani pH + pOH = 14. Neutral paani ke liye pH = pOH = 7.

book_ref.quote: These two quantities can be calculated as:

blocks.prompt:
23 A solution has [H⁺] = 4.0 × 10⁻⁹ mol dm⁻³. Find its pH and state whether it is acidic or basic.
(Aik solution mein [H⁺] = 4.0 × 10⁻⁹ mol dm⁻³ hai. Is ka pH nikalein aur batayein ke acidic hai ya basic.)
blocks.explanation: pH = −log(4.0 × 10⁻⁹) = 8.40. pH 7 se zyada hai, is liye solution basic hai.

book_ref.quote: This table can help you to understand the acidic or basic nature of commonly used solutions.

blocks.prompt:
24 The pH of a solution is 9.8 at 25 °C. Calculate its [OH⁻].
(25 °C par aik solution ka pH 9.8 hai. Is ki [OH⁻] nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Find the concentration of H⁺ and OH⁻, Taking antilog of pH and pOH

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Yaad rakhein: pH se [H⁺] milta hai aur pOH se [OH⁻]. Book ke Sample Problem 9.1 mein yeh ulat chhap gaya hai.

blocks.prompt:
25 Is the pH of every aqueous solution limited to the range 0-14? Explain.
(Kya har aqueous solution ka pH 0-14 ki range tak mehdood hai? Wazahat karein.)
blocks.explanation: Nahi. 25 °C par pH aam tor par 0 aur 14 ke darmiyan hota hai, magar manfi pH aur 14 se zyada pH wale solutions bhi maloom hain.

book_ref.quote: Solutions of negative pH and having values more than 14 are also known.

blocks.prompt:
26 What is Ka? What does its value tell us?
(Ka kya hai? Is ki qeemat hamein kya batati hai?)
blocks.explanation: Ka acid ka dissociation constant hai: HA + H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + A⁻ ke liye Ka = [H₃O⁺][A⁻]/[HA]. Yeh acid ki taqat ka miqdaari paimana hai: Ka jitna bara, acid utna strong.

book_ref.quote: The value of Ka called the dissociation constant of an acid

blocks.prompt:
27 Show how Ka is obtained from Kc for the ionization of a weak acid HA.
(Weak acid HA ki ionization ke liye Kc se Ka kaise milta hai, dikhayein.)
blocks.explanation:
HA + H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + A⁻; Kc = [H₃O⁺][A⁻]/[HA][H₂O].
Paani zyada hai, is liye Kc[H₂O] = [H₃O⁺][A⁻]/[HA]. Kc[H₂O] = Ka rakhne se Ka = [H₃O⁺][A⁻]/[HA].

book_ref.quote: Kc for the reversible reaction will be written as follows:

blocks.prompt:
28 How are acids classified on the basis of their Ka values?
(Ka ki qeemat ki bunyaad par acids ki darja bandi kaise hoti hai?)
blocks.explanation:
Ka < 10⁻³: weak acid.
Ka = 1 se 10⁻³: moderately strong acid.
Ka > 1: strong acid.

book_ref.quote: Ka = 1 to 10⁻³ acid is moderately strong.

blocks.prompt:
29 Which is the stronger acid, H₂CO₃ (Ka = 4.4 × 10⁻⁷) or H₂S (Ka = 1.0 × 10⁻⁷)? Give a reason.
(Kaun sa acid zyada strong hai, H₂CO₃ (Ka = 4.4 × 10⁻⁷) ya H₂S (Ka = 1.0 × 10⁻⁷)? Wajah batayein.)
blocks.explanation: H₂CO₃ zyada strong hai. Ka acid ki taqat ka paimana hai aur H₂CO₃ ka Ka bara hai (4.4 × 10⁻⁷ > 1.0 × 10⁻⁷), is liye yeh zyada ionize hota hai. Dono weak hain (Ka < 10⁻³).

book_ref.quote: The values of Ka for some acids are given in Table 9.3.

blocks.prompt:
30 Why is [H₃O⁺] in a weak acid solution not equal to the initial concentration of the acid?
(Weak acid solution mein [H₃O⁺] acid ki shuru ki concentration ke barabar kyun nahi hoti?)
blocks.explanation: Weak acids paani mein poori tarah dissociate nahi hote; HA ka thora sa hissa hi ionize hota hai. Is liye [H₃O⁺] shuru ki concentration se kam hoti hai aur equilibrium expression (Ka) se nikalni parti hai.

book_ref.quote: Therefore, the concentration of hydronium ions is not equal to the initial concentration of the acid.

blocks.prompt:
31 Derive the relation [H₃O⁺] ≈ √(Ka × C) for a weak acid.
(Weak acid ke liye [H₃O⁺] ≈ √(Ka × C) ka taaluq nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Equilibrium par [H₃O⁺] = [A⁻] = x aur [HA] = C − x, is liye Ka = x²/(C − x). Weak acid mein x C ke muqable mein bohat chhota hai, is liye C − x ≈ C aur Ka ≈ x²/C. Lehaza x = [H₃O⁺] ≈ √(Ka × C).

book_ref.quote: For weak acids, x is usually very small compared to C, so C – x ≈ C.

blocks.prompt:
32 Calculate [H₃O⁺] in 0.010 mol dm⁻³ acetic acid. (Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵)
(0.010 mol dm⁻³ acetic acid mein [H₃O⁺] nikalein. (Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵))

book_ref.quote: Taking the square root of both sides:

blocks.prompt:
33 A 0.020 mol dm⁻³ solution of a weak acid HA has [H₃O⁺] = 6.0 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³. Calculate Ka.
(Weak acid HA ke 0.020 mol dm⁻³ solution mein [H₃O⁺] = 6.0 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³ hai. Ka nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: This equation can be used to calculate Ka for any acidic solution if we know the pH or [H⁺] of that solution

blocks.prompt:
34 How is sodium chloride purified by passing HCl gas through brine? Give equations.
(Brine mein HCl gas guzaar kar sodium chloride kaise saaf kiya jata hai? Equations dein.)
blocks.explanation:
NaCl(s) ⇌ Na⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq); HCl(g) ⇌ H⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq).
HCl se [Cl⁻] barhti hai; equilibrium constant qaim rakhne ke liye Na⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) → NaCl(s), aur khalis NaCl ke crystals nikal aate hain.

book_ref.quote: We are familiar with purification of sodium chloride by passing hydrogen chloride gas through brine

blocks.prompt:
35 What happens to the unionized species when a common ion is added to a solution of a less soluble electrolyte?
(Kam hal hone wale electrolyte ke solution mein common ion dalne se unionized species par kya asar hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Common ion electrolyte ki ionization ko dabata hai, is liye unionized species ki concentration barhti hai aur yeh precipitate ban kar nikal sakti hai.

book_ref.quote: The addition of a common ion to the solution of a less soluble electrolyte suppresses its ionization

blocks.prompt:
36 Why does KClO₃ precipitate when KCl is added to its solution? Write equations.
(KClO₃ ke solution mein KCl dalne se KClO₃ precipitate kyun hota hai? Equations likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
KClO₃(s) ⇌ K⁺(aq) + ClO₃⁻(aq); KCl(s) ⇌ K⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq).
Zyada hal hone wala KCl common ion K⁺ deta hai, jo kam hal hone wale KClO₃ ki ionization dabata hai, is liye yeh precipitate ban kar baith jata hai.

book_ref.quote: K⁺ is a common ion. The ionization of KClO₃ is suppressed and it settles down as precipitate.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Book mein KClO₃ se ClO⁻ likha hai; durust chlorate ion ClO₃⁻ hai.

blocks.prompt:
37 Why is HCl added to H₂S in salt analysis of second group basic radicals?
(Doosre group ke basic radicals ke salt analysis mein H₂S ke saath HCl kyun dala jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: H₂S ⇌ 2H⁺ + S²⁻ aur HCl → H⁺ + Cl⁻. H⁺ common ion hai, is liye H₂S kam dissociate hota hai aur S²⁻ ki kam concentration banti hai. Yeh kam [S²⁻] doosre group ke basic radicals ko precipitate karti hai.

book_ref.quote: Similarly, the dissociation of a weak acid H₂S in water can be suppressed by the addition of stronger acid HCl.

blocks.prompt:
38 What is the role of NH₄Cl in NH₃ solution used for third group basic radicals?
(Teesre group ke basic radicals ke liye NH₃ solution mein NH₄Cl ka kya kirdaar hai?)
blocks.explanation: NH₄Cl strong electrolyte hai: NH₄Cl → NH₄⁺ + Cl⁻. Common ion NH₄⁺ ki bari miqdaar NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻ ko dabati hai aur [OH⁻] kam karti hai. Yeh mixture teesre group ke basic radicals ka group reagent hai.

book_ref.quote: An addition of NH₄Cl in NH₃ solution suppresses the concentration of OH⁻

blocks.prompt:
39 What are buffer solutions? Give one example.
(Buffer solutions kya hain? Aik misaal dein.)
blocks.explanation: Buffer solutions thora acid ya base dalne par apne pH ki tabdeeli ko rokte hain; patla karne ya rakhne se bhi pH nahi badalta. Misaal: acetic acid + sodium acetate.

book_ref.quote: The solutions which resist the change in their pH when a small amount of an acid or a base is added to them

blocks.prompt:
40 How is an acidic buffer prepared? What is its pH range?
(Acidic buffer kaise banaya jata hai? Is ka pH kitna hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Acidic buffer weak acid aur strong base ke saath us ke salt ko mila kar banta hai, maslan CH₃COOH + CH₃COONa. Aise buffers ka pH 7 se kam hota hai.

book_ref.quote: Such solutions give acidic buffers with pH less than 7.

blocks.prompt:
41 How does an acetic acid-sodium acetate buffer resist a change in pH when a little acid is added?
(Thora acid dalne par acetic acid-sodium acetate buffer pH ki tabdeeli ko kaise rokta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Buffer CH₃COOH aur CH₃COO⁻ ka bara zakheera hai. Shamil H₃O⁺ CH₃COO⁻ se react karta hai: CH₃COO⁻ + H₃O⁺ → CH₃COOH + H₂O. Weak acetic acid undissociated rehta hai, is liye pH taqreeban nahi badalta.

book_ref.quote: When an acid or H₃O⁺ ions are added to this buffer, they will react with CH₃COO⁻ to give back acetic acid

blocks.prompt:
42 Why does the pH of acetic acid solution increase when sodium acetate is added? Use Table 9.4.
(Acetic acid solution mein sodium acetate dalne se pH kyun barhta hai? Table 9.4 istemal karein.)
blocks.explanation: CH₃COONa common ion CH₃COO⁻ deta hai jo CH₃COOH ki dissociation dabata hai, is liye [H₃O⁺] kam hoti hai. Table 9.4 mein 0.10 mol dm⁻³ acid ka pH akele 2.89 aur 0.05, 0.10, 0.15 mol dm⁻³ acetate ke saath 4.44, 4.74, 4.92 hai.

book_ref.quote: If one goes on adding CH₃COONa in CH₃COOH solution

blocks.prompt:
43 Write Henderson's equation. Which two factors govern the pH of a buffer?
(Henderson ki equation likhein. Buffer ka pH kin do factors par munhasir hai?)
blocks.explanation: pH = pKa + log([Salt]/[Acid]). Buffer ka pH (i) istemal hone wale acid ke pKa aur (ii) salt aur acid ki concentrations ki nisbat par munhasir hai.

book_ref.quote: This relationship is called Henderson’s equation.

blocks.prompt:
44 Show that a buffer containing equal concentrations of acid and salt has pH = pKa.
(Dikhayein ke jis buffer mein acid aur salt ki concentrations barabar hon us ka pH = pKa hai.)
blocks.explanation: pH = pKa + log([Salt]/[Acid]). Agar [Salt] = [Acid] ho to log(1) = 0, is liye pH = pKa. Acetic acid-sodium acetate buffer ke liye pH = 4.74.

book_ref.quote: The best buffer is prepared by taking equal concentration of salt and acid.

blocks.prompt:
45 Calculate the pH of a buffer containing 0.30 mol dm⁻³ CH₃COOH and 0.10 mol dm⁻³ CH₃COONa. (pKa = 4.74)
(0.30 mol dm⁻³ CH₃COOH aur 0.10 mol dm⁻³ CH₃COONa wale buffer ka pH nikalein. (pKa = 4.74))

book_ref.quote: Interchanging the numerator and denominator, the sign of log changes.

blocks.text: 9.8 Solubility product (for slightly soluble ionic compounds)

blocks.prompt:
46 Derive the solubility product expression for PbSO₄.
(PbSO₄ ke solubility product ka expression nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: PbSO₄(s) ⇌ Pb²⁺(aq) + SO₄²⁻(aq); Kc = [Pb²⁺][SO₄²⁻]/[PbSO₄]. Bohat kam hal hone ki wajah se [PbSO₄] constant rehti hai, is liye Kc[PbSO₄] = Ksp = [Pb²⁺][SO₄²⁻] = 25 °C par 1.6 × 10⁻⁸.

book_ref.quote: Bring [PbSO₄] on L.H.S. with Kc.

blocks.prompt:
47 Write the Ksp expressions for Al(OH)₃ and CaF₂.
(Al(OH)₃ aur CaF₂ ke Ksp expressions likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
Al(OH)₃ ⇌ Al³⁺ + 3OH⁻: Ksp = [Al³⁺][OH⁻]³
CaF₂ ⇌ Ca²⁺ + 2F⁻: Ksp = [Ca²⁺][F⁻]²
(har concentration ko balanced equation ke coefficient ki power)

book_ref.quote: So, the solubility product is the product of the concentrations of ions raised to an exponent equal to the co-efficient of the balanced equation.

blocks.prompt:
48 How does the dissolution of NaCl differ from that of PbSO₄ in water?
(Paani mein NaCl ke hal hone aur PbSO₄ ke hal hone mein kya farq hai?)
blocks.explanation: NaCl poori tarah dissociate hota hai; PbSO₄ thora sa dissociate ho kar apne ions ke saath equilibrium mein rehta hai.

book_ref.quote: When a soluble ionic compound is dissolved in water, like NaCl, it dissociates completely into ions.

rows: Poori tarah Na⁺ aur Cl⁻ mein toot-ta hai.
Equilibrium par dissociation poori nahi hoti.
Solution mein sirf ions hote hain.
Solution mein Pb²⁺, SO₄²⁻ aur undissociated PbSO₄ hote hain.
Solubility product istemal nahi hota.
Ksp = [Pb²⁺][SO₄²⁻] = 1.6 × 10⁻⁸ se bayan hota hai.

blocks.prompt:
49 MgCO₃ has Ksp = 3.5 × 10⁻⁸ (Table 9.5). Calculate its molar solubility.
(MgCO₃ ka Ksp = 3.5 × 10⁻⁸ hai (Table 9.5). Is ki molar solubility nikalein.)
blocks.explanation:
MgCO₃ ⇌ Mg²⁺ + CO₃²⁻; [Mg²⁺] = [CO₃²⁻] = S
Ksp = S² = 3.5 × 10⁻⁸, S = √(3.5 × 10⁻⁸) = 1.9 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³

book_ref.quote: Then the unknown molar solubility S is calculated and the concentration of the ions is determined.

blocks.prompt:
50 The molar solubility of AgCl is 1.34 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³. Calculate its Ksp.
(AgCl ki molar solubility 1.34 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ hai. Is ka Ksp nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Table 9.6 shows the relationship between the Ksp values and the solubility of some sparingly soluble compounds.

blocks.prompt:
51 How does comparing the ionic product with Ksp predict precipitation?
(Ionic product ka Ksp se muqabla precipitate banne ki pesh goi kaise karta hai?)
blocks.explanation:
Ionic product > Ksp: supersaturated solution, precipitate banta hai.
Ionic product = Ksp: saturated, precipitate nahi.
Ionic product < Ksp: unsaturated, precipitate nahi.

book_ref.quote: The solubility product can also help in predicting whether the precipitation of a salt will occur or not.

blocks.prompt:
52 After mixing, a solution has [Pb²⁺] = [SO₄²⁻] = 1.0 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³. Will PbSO₄ (Ksp = 1.6 × 10⁻⁸) precipitate?
(Milane ke baad aik solution mein [Pb²⁺] = [SO₄²⁻] = 1.0 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ hai. Kya PbSO₄ (Ksp = 1.6 × 10⁻⁸) precipitate hoga?)
blocks.explanation:
Ionic product = (1.0 × 10⁻³)² = 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ mol² dm⁻⁶
1.0 × 10⁻⁶ > 1.6 × 10⁻⁸, is liye solution supersaturated hai aur PbSO₄ precipitate hota hai.

blocks.prompt:
53 How does a nautilus form its shell from seawater, in terms of precipitation?
(Nautilus samandari paani se apna khol kaise banata hai, precipitation ke hawale se?)
blocks.explanation: Khol zyada tar calcium carbonate hai. Nautilus halaat aise banata hai ke Ca²⁺ aur CO₃²⁻ ki concentrations kaafi zyada hon (ionic product Ksp se barh jaye) aur CaCO₃ khol ki shakal mein precipitate ho.

book_ref.quote: The nautilus adjusts conditions so shell material is formed

blocks.prompt:
54 What is meant by salt hydrolysis?
(Salt hydrolysis se kya muraad hai?)
blocks.explanation: Salt paani mein hal ho kar apne ions mein toot-ta hai. Yeh ions paani se react kar ke solution ka pH badal sakte hain, is baat par munhasir ke salt kis acid aur base se bana hai.

book_ref.quote: When a salt dissolves in water, it dissociates into its constituent ions.

blocks.prompt:
55 Why is an aqueous solution of NaCl neutral?
(NaCl ka aqueous solution neutral kyun hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: NaCl → Na⁺ + Cl⁻. Na⁺ strong base NaOH ka bohat weak conjugate acid aur Cl⁻ strong acid HCl ka bohat weak conjugate base hai. Koi bhi paani se khaas react nahi karta, is liye pH nahi badalta aur solution neutral rehta hai.

book_ref.quote: The conjugate acid of a strong base (e.g., Na⁺ from NaOH) is also very weak and does not significantly react with water.

blocks.prompt:
56 Why is an aqueous solution of NH₄Cl acidic? Give the equation.
(NH₄Cl ka aqueous solution acidic kyun hota hai? Equation dein.)
blocks.explanation: NH₄⁺ (weak base NH₃ ka conjugate acid) paani se react karta hai: NH₄⁺(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ NH₃ + H₃O⁺(aq). Cl⁻ (strong HCl se) react nahi karta. Banne wala H₃O⁺ solution ko acidic karta hai.

book_ref.quote: NH₄⁺ is the conjugate acid of NH₃ (a weak base) and reacts with water:

blocks.prompt:
57 Why is an aqueous solution of sodium acetate basic? Give the equation.
(Sodium acetate ka aqueous solution basic kyun hota hai? Equation dein.)
blocks.explanation: CH₃COO⁻ (weak acid CH₃COOH ka conjugate base) paani se react karta hai: CH₃COO⁻(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ CH₃COOH(aq) + OH⁻(aq). Na⁺ pH par asar nahi daalta. Banne wala OH⁻ solution ko basic karta hai.

book_ref.quote: The example of salt of weak acid and strong base is sodium acetate.

blocks.prompt:
58 Why may a solution of ammonium acetate be acidic, basic or nearly neutral?
(Ammonium acetate ka solution acidic, basic ya taqreeban neutral kyun ho sakta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Dono ions hydrolyze hote hain: NH₄⁺ + H₂O ⇌ NH₃ + H₃O⁺ se H₃O⁺ aur CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COOH + OH⁻ se OH⁻ banta hai. pH conjugate acid aur conjugate base ki nisbati taqat par munhasir hai, yani kaun sa reaction ghalib hai.

book_ref.quote: The solution may be acidic, basic, or nearly neutral, depending on which reaction is more dominant.

blocks.prompt:
59 Differentiate between the hydrolysis of NH₄Cl and of CH₃COONa.
(NH₄Cl aur CH₃COONa ke hydrolysis mein farq bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation: NH₄Cl mein cation hydrolyze ho kar H₃O⁺ deta hai; CH₃COONa mein anion hydrolyze ho kar OH⁻ deta hai.

book_ref.quote: For salts derived from strong acids and weak bases (e.g., ammonium chloride, NH₄Cl)

rows: Strong acid aur weak base ka salt.
Weak acid aur strong base ka salt.
Cation NH₄⁺ paani se react karta hai.
Anion CH₃COO⁻ paani se react karta hai.
NH₄⁺ + H₂O ⇌ NH₃ + H₃O⁺
CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COOH + OH⁻
Solution acidic hai.
Solution basic hai.

blocks.prompt:
60 Why does a weak-acid indicator HIn show two different colours?
(Weak-acid indicator HIn do alag rang kyun dikhata hai?)
blocks.explanation: HIn ⇌ H⁺ + In⁻. Reaction reversible hai, is liye HIn aur In⁻ dono maujood hote hain aur dono ke rang alag hain. Nazar aane wala rang kisi pH par un ki nisbati miqdaar par munhasir hai.

blocks.prompt:
61 Why is an indicator present mainly as HIn in acid and as In⁻ in base?
(Indicator acid mein zyada tar HIn aur base mein In⁻ kyun hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Acid mein In⁻ ions Bronsted bases ban kar proton lete hain, is liye unionized HIn ghalib hota hai. Base mein OH⁻ indicator ka H⁺ hata deta hai, is liye mazeed HIn ionize hota hai aur In⁻ ghalib hota hai (maslan litmus neela).

book_ref.quote: In acidic solutions, any In⁻ ions that are present act as Brønsted bases and accept protons from the acid.

blocks.prompt:
62 What is meant by the range of an indicator? Give the example of methyl red.
(Indicator ki range se kya muraad hai? Methyl red ki misaal dein.)
blocks.explanation: Har indicator aik muqarrar pH range (taqreeban 2 pH units) mein rang badalta hai, jise indicator range kehte hain. Methyl red pH 4.4 aur 6.2 ke darmiyan laal se peela hota hai; pH 4.4 par zyada tar laal HIn hota hai.

book_ref.quote: For example, methyl red changes from red to yellow between pH 4.4 and 6.2.

blocks.prompt:
63 State the two general criteria for selecting an indicator for a titration.
(Titration ke liye indicator chunne ki do aam sharait bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation:
(1) Titration ke aakhir ka pH indicator ke neutral point (rang badalne ki range) ke qareeb ho.
(2) Indicator equivalence point ke qareeb tez rang ki tabdeeli dikhaye.

blocks.prompt:
64 Differentiate between equivalence point and end point of a titration.
(Titration ke equivalence point aur end point mein farq bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation: Equivalence point miqdaaron ke poora react hone se aata hai; end point indicator ke rang badalne se nazar aata hai.

book_ref.quote: The equivalence point is the point at which the amount of titrant added is just enough to neutralize the analyte solution completely.

rows: Shamil titrant analyte ko poori tarah neutral karne ke liye bilkul kaafi hota hai.
Woh point jahan indicator rang badalta hai.
Acid aur base ki miqdaaron (stoichiometry) se tay hota hai.
Chune gaye indicator par munhasir hai.
Titration curve ke tez (steep) hisse se milta hai.
Titration ke dauran flask mein seedha nazar aata hai.
Titration ka asal (ideal) point.
Equivalence point ke qareeb hona chahiye.

blocks.prompt:
65 What is a pH curve? What is plotted on its axes?
(pH curve kya hai? Is ke axes par kya dikhaya jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: pH (titration) curve solution ke pH ko shamil titrant ke volume ke muqable mein dikhata hai. Is se pata chalta hai ke acidic ya basic solution mein base ya acid dalne par pH kaise badalta hai; pH khari (vertical) axis par aur titrant ka volume leti (horizontal) axis par.

book_ref.quote: Titration curves show how the pH of an acidic or basic solution changes as a basic or acidic solution is added to it.

blocks.prompt:
66 Why can phenolphthalein be used in the titration of HCl with NaOH?
(HCl ki NaOH se titration mein phenolphthalein kyun istemal ho sakta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Strong acid-strong base titration ke equivalence point par pH 7.0 hota hai aur pH taqreeban 4.0 se 10.0 tak tezi se barhta hai. Phenolphthalein isi tez range mein rang badalta hai, is liye end point zahir karta hai.

book_ref.quote: These titrations have a pH of 7.0 at equivalence, so, such phenolphthalein as indicator can be used

blocks.prompt:
67 Why is the pH at the equivalence point of an NH₃-HCl titration less than 7?
(NH₃-HCl titration ke equivalence point par pH 7 se kam kyun hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Equivalence point par solution mein NH₄⁺ hota hai, jo weak base ka conjugate acid hai. Yeh thora sa dissociate hota hai, NH₄⁺ → NH₃ + H⁺, aur H⁺ ions deta hai, is liye solution acidic hai (pH = 5.27).

book_ref.quote: because the conjugate acid slightly dissociates, releasing H⁺ ions making the solution acidic

blocks.prompt:
68 Why is methyl orange used for strong acid-weak base titrations?
(Strong acid-weak base titrations ke liye methyl orange kyun istemal hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Strong acid-weak base titration ka equivalence point acidic hisse (pH 5.27) mein hota hai aur phir pH tezi se girta hai. Methyl orange isi acidic range (3.2-4.5) mein rang badalta hai, is liye end point deta hai.

book_ref.quote: Methyl orange has its colour change in this range, therefore, it can be used as an indicator for strong acid-weak base titrations.

blocks.prompt:
69 Compare a strong acid-strong base titration with a strong acid-weak base titration.
(Strong acid-strong base titration ka strong acid-weak base titration se muqabla karein.)
blocks.explanation: Dono mein equivalence point ka pH, buffer region aur indicator mukhtalif hain.

book_ref.quote: Consider the titration of aqueous NH₃ with HCl.
